method: Fresh Chrome profiles; local static server; 15 seconds warmup; 2.5 seconds settling then 6.5 seconds sampled per location. CPU profiler enabled equally in before/after. Adaptive resolution retained. Final desktop run performed without concurrent test jobs.
changes: Eden no longer constructs, shader-compiles or uploads hidden combat/night worlds during browsing. Their existing doorway loading screen owns initialization.
The library no longer triggers construction of the night district by proximity.
Projected HUD labels use cached viewport measurements, avoiding forced layout every frame.

Portal interiors stay hidden outside portal passes; targets use 8-bit color and quantized distance-scaled resolution with a resize cooldown. Stationary portals refresh at 30 fps; movement refreshes immediately.

Rack models stream serially, pause when the visitor leaves, and resume on return. Display texture dimensions are capped at 1024 before staged GPU upload; original geometry and separate inspection models are retained.
The jester shares the world environment map; daytime Eden no longer prebakes five night sky environments.
Static museum exterior meshes join existing geometry batching. Idle preparation respects active input, visibility and spare frame time.

validation.nativeCombat: Passed cold Beyond Eden entry, real pointer lock, 3 pistol shots, reload, stronger assisted hit, armed momentum HUD, aerial stomp and ground tackle; no runtime exceptions.

movement.knownExistingFailure: A jump just after walking off an edge still works: left=false, upSpeed=0. Previously reproduced on unchanged source; shared movement code was not modified.

limitations: These are short, local desktop measurements, not a guarantee of 60 fps on every device or network.
The mobile run emulates a viewport on the same M3, not phone GPU/CPU performance.
Initial garden camera motion and resident positions vary slightly; library, museum and return viewpoints are fixed.
Rack assets load during museum sampling, so garment count and draw calls vary with timing. Museum timing is an end-to-end loading result, not a fixed geometry benchmark.
Startup time is not used as a headline comparison because driver caches and resource timing vary.
GPU texture counts are object counts, not VRAM byte measurements. Full-route long tasks fell from 50 to 16, but transient stalls still exist.
Multiplayer backend load and live audio were not benchmarked by the static-server route.
